item.title: Bizarre! Ali Khan's wide ball goes for six, batter gets only five runs - Watch
item.description: A bizarre incident in the Canada's premier T10 cricket league semi-final saw Ali Khan’s wide bouncer clear the boundary, but Toronto Sixers received only five runs. Under MCC laws, a ball not hit by the bat counts as four, plus one for the wide. Toronto beat Mississauga Masters by nine runs and reached the final, where they will face Vancouver Anchors.
item.dc:creator: JYOTIRMOY HALDER

item.title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
item.description: In a surprising blunder, US President Donald Trump claimed that 125 million individuals participated in India's presidential election, sparking confusion given Brazil's recent electoral events. His remarks drew attention to his concerns over the integrity of the US electoral system. Social media users quickly slammed the President and highlighted inaccuracies in his understanding of India’s election process.
item.dc:creator: KANCHAN YADAV

item.title: Elon Musk admits that Tesla Robotaxis have a 'cat problem'
item.description: Tesla's Robotaxi service has recently broadened its operational hours, now extending to 11 PM. However, it faces challenges with low-light detection, particularly struggling to identify small creatures like grey kittens in dark conditions. Elon Musk acknowledged the drawbacks of relying solely on cameras at a promotional event. In contrast, companies like Waymo incorporate various sensors, including lidar, to enhance their visibility.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Mizoram woman left teaching for farming; now she is being honoured by UN
item.description: Z T Lalrithangi hails from Sangau and initially struggled to secure a government job post-education. Redirecting her passion, she delved into strawberry farming, ultimately cultivating over 10,000 plants from her original 1,000 in just a few years. Her remarkable journey has earned her a spot among the FAO's 100 Women Heroes, highlighting her path to empowerment and financial independence through agriculture.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: Man sells ancestral land for Rs 8 cr, claims LTCG; tax dept rejects & adds Rs 6.36 cr
item.description: In the tax return that he filed, the man declared LTCG of Rs 7.73 crore after accounting for certain expenses. He claimed tax exemptions of Rs 2.64 crore under Section 54F, which relates to residential property, and Section 54B, applicable to agricultural property. However, the Assessing Officer (AO) was not satisfied with the documents that were submitted by the taxpayer to support his claims
item.dc:creator: TOI BUSINESS DESK

item.title: Can CEC Gyanesh Kumar exercise EC powers alone? SC to hear plea today
item.description: On Monday, the Supreme Court is set to hear pleas regarding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's alleged misuse of authority. The petitions argue that Kumar acted without the approval of fellow commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi. They seek to suspend Kumar until the case is resolved while allowing Sandhu and Joshi to jointly manage commission tasks.
item.dc:creator: SAURABH THAKUR

item.title: SC issues notice to Centre over Central Vista library plan, seeks reply in 3 weeks
item.description: The Supreme Court has urged the Centre to submit a comprehensive report regarding library facilities. The inquiry centers on the designated space for the current book collection within the Central Vista project framework. Since 2011, around two lakh books have been stored without being unpacked, prompting worries from court officials.
item.dc:creator: ARYAN SINGH

item.title: Delhi riots: HC rejects pleas seeking FIRs against political leaders over 'hate speeches'
item.dc:creator: KANCHAN YADAV

item.title: Michigan collector paid $30 for painting; it later sold for record $1.35 million
item.description: In a stunning turn of events, Gertrude Abercrombie's painting, Alderman Merriam's Shells, was auctioned for $1,352,600 after being found at an estate sale for just $30. Having been lost for 75 years, the piece drew significant attention at Freeman's auction house, far exceeding expectations. A dedicated collector meticulously verified its authenticity, marking a remarkable resurgence for Abercrombie in the contemporary art scene.
item.dc:creator: TIMESOFINDIA.COM

item.title: IAF seeks to use a multi-pronged approach to arrest falling fighter strength
item.description: The Indian Air Force chief has highlighted the ongoing shortage of fighter aircraft within the organization. The current fleet consists of 29 fighter squadrons, much lower than the authorized strength. Efforts are underway to expedite the production of the Tejas Mark-1A and finalize the 114-aircraft Multi-Role Fighter Aircraft deal. Additionally, the Air Force is considering procuring fifth-generation fighters if domestic production experiences delays.
item.dc:creator: DHRUV YADAV

item.title: Marc Benioff, wife gave $100M to UCSF; 5 years later, children’s hospital opened
item.description: Marc Benioff and Lynne Benioff significantly contributed $100 million to UCSF for a new children's hospital. This hospital opened in February 2015, featuring advanced facilities designed exclusively for pediatric care. In addition, they made another $100 million donation in 2014 to further support pediatric research and clinical programs. The hospitals were renamed to honor the Benioffs for their generous contributions to children's health care.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Complainant gets Rs 1.63L payout after scooter failed to deliver promised mileage
item.description: A consumer commission in Kerala ruled in favor of a customer regarding an electric scooter. The customer experienced multiple defects, including poor battery performance and a defective wheel bearing system. After the commission's investigation, they found the manufacturer's service insufficient and defective. The company was ordered to refund Rs 88,000 and pay additional compensation and litigation costs. The manufacturer must comply within 45 days or face further financial penalties.
item.dc:creator: SAURABH THAKUR

item.title: Bihar cop suspended after video shows him brandishing pistol at flood-hit people
item.description: Sangram Kumar Singh, the station house officer of Maker Police Station in Bihar, was suspended for indiscipline. He was filmed brandishing a pistol while distributing flood relief materials to affected citizens. The incident was widely circulated on social media, prompting an official statement from Saran's police department. Almost 9.87 lakh people faced distress due to the floods impacting multiple districts.
item.dc:creator: LAIRENLAKPAM WARLI

item.title: Noida man held for 'molestation' at Kolkata hotel after Brazil match
item.description: A man from Noida was arrested for allegedly molesting two women in a Kolkata hotel lobby. The incident occurred shortly after a football match between Brazil and India. Police reviewed CCTV footage and identified the accused, Palash Ray, in the hotel. Ray denied the allegations, claiming any contact was accidental, and investigations are ongoing. The statements of the victims and witnesses will be recorded as part of the inquiry.
item.dc:creator: DWAIPAYAN GHOSH

item.title: 3 years after Oct 7, Israel honours officer whose Hamas attack warning was ignored
item.description: An intelligence officer from Israel's Unit 8200 has been acknowledged for issuing multiple warnings regarding the Hamas invasion prior to the catastrophic attack on October 7, 2023. Unfortunately, those alerts went unheeded, which led to a coordinated assault from Gaza, resulting in heavy casualties and numerous hostages. This incident has led to a critical examination of the systemic shortcomings within Israel's military intelligence operations.
item.dc:creator: ARYAN SINGH

item.title: Rupee hovers near 96 as oil stays above $100 per barrel, foreign selling persists
item.description: The rupee started off on a weaker note against the US dollar due to soaring crude oil prices and foreign investors selling off. In response, the Reserve Bank of India is stepping in to curb volatile changes, as forex reserves dwindle. Market analysts anticipate a possible interest rate increase following the upcoming monetary policy meeting, while the dollar index remains robust.
item.dc:creator: SHIVANGHI PAYAL

item.title: Watch: Uruguay footballers play cricket at Eden Gardens ahead of Kolkata friendly
item.description: Uruguay’s football team explored Kolkata ahead of its October 6 friendly against India. The two-time World Cup champions visited Victoria Memorial and St Paul’s Cathedral and also tried cricket at Eden Gardens. The venue holds historical significance, as Uruguay won the 1982 Nehru Cup there. The squad, coached by Diego Forlán, will now prepare for the India clash.
item.dc:creator: JYOTIRMOY HALDER

item.title: Canada ‘looking forward’ to seal trade deal with India as fifth CEPA round begins
item.description: India and Canada are gearing up for the fifth session of negotiations on the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement, which will take place in Ottawa. The objective is to wrap up the trade deal by late 2026, with priority given to collaboration in sectors like energy, critical minerals, aerospace, and artificial intelligence.
item.dc:creator: SHIVANGHI PAYAL

item.title: Protesters climb barricades, confront police in march against Gyanesh; 120 detained
item.description: Protesters in New Delhi faced police resistance while demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. They gathered at multiple locations, pushing barricades and confronting police efforts to disperse the crowd. Allegations of police misconduct surfaced, including claims of inappropriate touching of women protesters. AISA reported that their president, Neha Bora, was taken away by male police officers without badges.
item.dc:creator: MEGHNA DHULIA

item.title: 'Never my intention to hurt': Sanjay Dutt on his India peace remark
item.description: Sanjay Dutt faced backlash for his comments about the lack of peace in India during a talk show. He clarified that his remarks were intended to be humorous and not offensive. Dutt expressed concern for the country's current state while praising the generosity of Indians. During the show, he humorously addressed the relationship between leadership and citizens.
item.dc:creator: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK

item.title: Texas city to pay at least $175,000 over excess groundwater pumping at SpaceX site
item.description: The McGregor City Council has reached a settlement regarding penalties related to groundwater overpumping caused by SpaceX. The city will allocate $175,000 for this resolution and commit to a 25-year groundwater monitoring program. However, residents are concerned about who will bear these costs, urging that SpaceX should take financial responsibility.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: 'Shameful': AAP shares video, says Delhi Police ‘abusing’ protesters at Jantar Mantar

item.title: CEC Gyanesh Kumar faces fresh Kerala vigilance probe in 2006 corruption case
item.description: In a bold move, Keralam's home minister Ramesh Chennithala has called for a renewed inquiry into a decades-old corruption case linked to chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and a World Bank road initiative. The case gained notoriety after Malaysian engineer Lee See Been reportedly ended his life amid claims of harassment by public works officials.
item.dc:creator: RAJIV G

item.title: SIR strikes at heart of Constitution: Supreme Court judge Ujjal Bhuyan
item.description: Justice Ujjal Bhuyan condemned the extensive deletion of voter names from electoral rolls due to the special intensive revision process. He emphasized that such actions undermine the core principles of the Indian Constitution and disenfranchise millions of citizens. Bhuyan highlighted that the right to vote is essential for free and fair elections in India. He urged that no citizen should be denied the right to vote without due process.
item.dc:creator: DHANANJAY MAHAPATRA

item.title: ‘Govt planning to arrest us’: Saurav Das calls for biggest mobilisation from Oct 10
item.description: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leaders announced plans for protests starting October 10 against perceived government repression. Saurav Das alleged government intentions to arrest him and other prominent leaders involved in activism. The protests are in response to an alleged incident of police misconduct against a woman journalist. CJP representatives demanded accountability from Delhi Police for their actions during demonstrations.
item.dc:creator: LAIRENLAKPAM WARLI

item.title: No classes in 500 schools on Monday: Why are France students protesting
item.description: In response to escalating student protests regarding education quality, France is set to close up to 500 high schools. Students are advocating for enhanced teaching staff and better resources to combat overcrowding and failing infrastructures. The unrest has led to significant clashes between police and demonstrators, prompting numerous arrests. Amid this turmoil, the government has vowed to enhance educational facilities and maintain classes.
item.dc:creator: ARYAN SINGH

item.title: Abducted Kuki farmer found dead with hands tied in Manipur's Kangpokpi
item.description: The body of 71-year-old Kuki farmer Hemjang Haokip was recovered from a forest in Manipur's Kangpokpi district. He was allegedly abducted from his field hut, which was later set on fire. Local authorities believe he was tortured and beaten to death based on the condition of his body. Community leaders described the killing as a pre-planned murder and condemned the suspected involvement of NSCN-IM militants.
item.dc:creator: KANGKAN KALITA

item.title: 'That's an irony when you look at him': Iyer makes honest Sooryavanshi admission
item.description: India T20I captain Shreyas Iyer praised teenage star Vaibhav Sooryavanshi ahead of the West Indies series, highlighting his quiet personality off the field and aggressive batting style. Iyer said Sooryavanshi’s opportunity will come despite established openers currently occupying the spots. The youngster, an Asian Games gold medallist, has already impressed in the IPL and international cricket.
item.dc:creator: JYOTIRMOY HALDER

item.title: Nikkei jumps 2.5% above 70,000 to three-month high as AI stocks rally
item.description: Japan's Nikkei index experienced a remarkable rise of over 2% on Monday, breaking the 70,000 mark for the first time in three months. The surge was largely driven by chip manufacturers like Tokyo Electron and Advantest, while Kioxia's contribution fell short. The optimistic trend in Japanese stocks was fueled by Wall Street's strong performance, stemming from weaker US jobs data alleviating rate hike anxieties.
item.dc:creator: SHIVANGHI PAYAL

item.title: Telangana woman dies in US after car-truck crash
item.description: Daram Supriya, a 31-year-old resident of Telangana, has met with a heartbreaking fate in Missouri, where she died in a road accident. The fatal crash happened late Saturday when a truck collided with her car as she was driving home from her restaurant. Her friend suffered grave injuries in the incident. Her family in India is appealing for help to bring Supriya's body back for her last rites.
item.dc:creator: SHIVA KUMAR PINNA

item.title: 'You can't just depend on Bumrah, Hardik': Ex-India cricketer urges veterans' return
item.description: Former India batter Hanuma Vihari urged India to recall Bhuvneshwar Kumar and Mohammed Shami after the team failed to defend 351 against West Indies. He warned against relying too heavily on Jasprit Bumrah and Hardik Pandya, calling the bowling performance a wake-up call. Vihari believes experience and stronger backup options are crucial with the 2027 World Cup approaching.
item.dc:creator: JYOTIRMOY HALDER

item.title: Flydubai co-pilot allegedly tried to crash plane after hijack attempt failed
item.description: An Omani co-pilot attacked the captain of a flydubai flight bound for Tel Aviv. Following the assault, he attempted to crash the aircraft into the Saudi desert. Investigators are looking into whether the co-pilot cut the engines' fuel supply during this crisis. Emergency codes were transmitted to air traffic control indicating both a general emergency and a suspected hijacking.
item.dc:creator: YASHASVI VASISTHA

item.title: ‘War isn’t over’: Al Qaeda calls for 'copycat attacks' after flydubai incident
item.dc:creator: AADRITA HALDER

item.title: Flydubai cockpit attack: How a family waited anxiously to see their injured son
item.description: Captain Smit Machchhar was injured during a terrorist attack and underwent surgery in a military hospital. His parents initially faced uncertainty regarding his condition while trying to reach him. After being airlifted to Abu Dhabi, Smit's father felt relieved upon visiting him. The family decided to focus on Smit's recovery instead of revisiting the traumatic event. They remain optimistic about his healing process and future homecoming.
item.dc:creator: HEMALI CHHAPIA AND MANJU V

item.title: Faster registration, easier refunds: Reform rollout with GST 2.0
item.description: GST Council plans to unveil substantial reforms aimed at improving business processes and facilitating growth. The proposed changes involve streamlined registration, easier refunds, and a more efficient input tax credit system. Decriminalisation measures are also proposed to alleviate issues for businesses with minor offenses. A focus is on reducing discretionary practices and using technology to minimize litigation. These reforms seek to enhance operational efficiency for both small and large enterprises.
item.dc:creator: SIDHARTHA

item.title: US military kills 4 in strike on suspected drug-trafficking vessel in Caribbean
item.dc:creator: AYUSH PANDEY

item.title: 'I had fever': R Praggnanandhaa after double medals at Chess Olympiad | Exclusive
item.description: In the fifth instalment of TimesofIndia.com's series on India's medal-winning Chess Olympiad campaigns in Samarkand, R Praggnanandhaa reflects on India's silver-medal finish and his individual bronze. The 21-year-old discusses battling illness, missed winning chances, the decisive defeat to Uzbekistan, the team's resilience, his recovery from the Candidates disappointment, and much more.
item.dc:creator: JYOTIRMOY HALDER
